messages:
marta: quick idea — propose an "auto-diversion" policy for saturated primaries. When a customer's pinned model is at capacity, route new requests to the next compatible variant automatically instead of queueing. keeps apps working and avoids tail latency spikes.
jamal: clarify: this is capacity-based, not quality-based, right? so we only trigger when serving pool reports saturation signals?
marta: yes. signals = queue depth, GPU util, request rejection rate from runtime. can't be purely latency percentiles because of noise.
priya: love the UX angle. in console we need a toggle per-tenant + opt-out at route level. default should be OFF for enterprise customers with strict model pinning.
alex: runtime note — variants must be binary-compatible (tokenizer + spec) or we need a conversion layer. otherwise responses break callers. we should require a manifest flag: "compatible_with" list.
kai: telemetry: we need a metric for diverted_count, diversion_rate_by_tier, and per-variant quality-delta hooks (sampled responses). otherwise product won't trust it.
sam: cost: if diversion sends to a larger model as fallback, spend could spike. policy should support cost caps and a preferred-variant list sorted by (cost, latency, quality).
marta: agree. suggested policy shape (very rough):
```json
{
  "trigger": {
    "type": "capacity",
    "thresholds": {"queue_depth": 50, "reject_rate": 0.02}
  },
  "candidates": ["gptx-std-q4", "gptx-std-int8"],
  "priority": "tier-awareness", 
  "controls": {"max_diversion_per_min": 1000, "cost_budget": 0.2}
}
```
priya: console UX: show predicted cost delta before enabling. preview a sample of diverted responses (redacted) with accept/deny. also surface per-route historical diversions and SLA impacts.
jamal: sdk/edge: need headers so clients know diversion happened (e.g., X-Redwood-Diverted: true, variant: gptx-std-int8). helps caller fallbacks or telemetry.
alex: what about function-calling and tooling? diverted variant must support function-calling semantics identically. otherwise we should fallback to rejecting the request or returning a deprecation warning.
kai: sampling for quality checks: route 1% of diverted responses to an evaluation pipeline to compute BLEU/ROUGE/LL-model-score vs golden prompts. store diffs.
sam: suggest tier-aware throttling: free tier -> prefer cheaper variants, platinum -> prefer low-latency variants, but allow override in tenant config.
priya: rollout plan: start with internal tenants, then opt-in beta for 10 customers, monitor diversion_rate, quality_regressions, and billing surprises for 2 weeks.
marta: API public change: introduce field in deployment policy "diversion_policy" and an API to preview candidate variants + estimated unit-cost. keep backward compatibility by default-off.
jamal: runtime integration: runtime will emit an event when variant is saturated: {model, pool_id, reason, ts}. router subscribes and computes diversion sets. need idempotency and debounce to avoid flapping.
kai: for telemetry naming: redwood.diversions.count, redwood.diversions.by_tier, redwood.diversions.quality_regressions. attach tags: tenant_id, route, primary_variant, fallback_variant.
alex: edge-case: in cross-region failover, prefer local variant replicas first. avoid cold start in other region. so policy must honor region affinity.
priya: console control: single-click revert and an audit trail entry for each automatic diversion enabling. compliance teams will want the audit.
sam: question about quotas: if primary is throttling because tenant hit quota, should we divert? I think no — quota exceedance means customer shouldn't get more tokens. diverting would silently bypass quota.
marta: good call — diversion must NOT bypass tenant-specific quotas. treat quota blocks as hard-stop. diversion only for infra saturation. add explicit check in router.
jamal: can we add a per-route "diversion_sensitivity" param: "strict" (only identical variants), "lenient" (allow lower-quality cheaper variants)? product might want that.
kai: we should also add circuit-breaker: if diverted responses fail quality checks above threshold, auto-disable diversion for that tenant and notify SE.
deploy-bot: deployment queued: feature flag "auto_diversion_v1" scheduled to canary in dev tomorrow at 08:00 UTC.
priya: notifications: plan to email account owners when diversion > 5% for 24h. also Slack alert to #customer-health for enterprise customers.
marta: next steps: draft schema for diversion_policy (JSON schema), runtime events spec, console mockups, and a beta rollout checklist. volunteers?
jamal: I'll take runtime events + router debounce design.
priya: I'll do console mockups + rollout flows.
kai: I'll own telemetry & sampling pipelines.
alex: I'll write the compatibility manifest proposal and SDK headers.
sam: I'll draft cost-guard rules and quota interactions doc.
marta: perfect — let's sync tomorrow 10am. thanks all :thumbsup:
